subject: Production 429s — capacity tiering mismatch causing retry runaways
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medistream.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@medistream.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 06:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 429s + downstream timeouts (start 05:58 PDT)

Diego / Marissa —

We began seeing a sustained spike of 429s against your generation endpoint for our org (msh-prod) starting ~05:58 PDT. Latency also climbed and our frontend started timing out after a cascade of retries. Traffic pattern was normal for us (no deploys this morning) — attached are a short sample of request ids and a CSV of our observed client-side accept rate.

Immediate impact: several clinical workflows failed to complete (non-blocking for now but high severity from product).

What we need: confirmation this is on your side, a short mitigation (temporary quota bump or fallback to previous tier), and ETA for root cause. We are pausing aggressive retries on our side but the burst continues.

Attached: msh-429-sample-logs.txt, rate-config-diff.csv

—Karen Liu
Sr. Platform PM, MediStream Health
karen.liu@medistream.com
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medistream.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 06:24:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s + downstream timeouts (start 05:58 PDT)

Karen — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. I'm triaging now and looping in infra (Aditya) + account lead (Marissa).

Short answer: we see the same 429 surge from our edge and a matching increase in org-level quota rejections. I'm putting an emergency bypass in place now (5m window) to let your traffic through while we diagnose. Can you confirm any recent changes on your end to project/organization keys or rate-limit tiers?

I'll update in the next 15 minutes with telemetry and exact mitigation steps.

—Diego
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 06:31:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s + downstream timeouts (start 05:58 PDT)

On our side: preliminary traces show the 429s are predominantly originating from org-level enforcement rather than per-project limits. There was a recent automated tier reconciliation at 05:50 that incorrectly reset a subset of MediStream projects to a lower capacity tier because two project IDs were merged in billing — this reduced the aggregated allowance and caused a quota cutover when traffic ramped.

Immediate action taken:
- Applied temporary org quota override for msh-prod (effective immediately)
- Disabled aggressive client-side retry guidance in the short term via config flag (reduces retry storms)
- Opened an internal patch to fix reconciliation logic (INF-4821)

Next steps for ops: Aditya suggests Medistream pause any bulk job retries for 30 minutes and confirm which project keys map to the merged billing entity so we can reconcile properly.

I'll stay on the thread while we watch for stabilization.

—Aditya (Infra Eng Lead)
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medistream.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@medistream.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 06:39:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s + downstream timeouts (start 05:58 PDT)

Thanks Diego / Aditya. We just confirmed two of our deploys this morning re-pointed traffic to a consolidated project token as part of an internal cost-center cleanup — that likely explains the merged IDs. We're pausing retries now.

Please keep the override in place and let us know when it's safe to resume. We need a short post-incident note for our ops page with root cause and exact TTL of the override. ETA on the reconciliation patch?

—Karen
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medistream.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 07:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s + downstream timeouts (start 05:58 PDT)

Quick update: traffic has returned to baseline following the override and your retry pause. We left the temporary override for 60 minutes to ensure no residual backpressure. Infra has a patch scheduled and we expect a permanent fix in the control-plane reconciliation flow in the next 6–8 hours (INF-4821).

Deliverables I'll own:
- Post-incident summary (root cause + timeline) — by EOD PST
- Confirmation of reorder of project mappings and permanent config change — within 8 hours
- Credits/SL considerations if you want formal review, loop in Marissa on next steps for commercial relief.

Appreciate the quick confirmation from your side.

—Diego
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Spike in 429s + downstream timeouts (start 05:58 PDT)

Thanks team — good containment on quick mitigation. A few follow-ups for leadership and Legal:
- Diego: include the exact override window start/end in the post-incident note and list impacted project IDs.
- Marissa: please prepare a note for the account that includes any short-term credit offer (we should be conservative but empathetic).
- Aditya: confirm whether the reconciliation fix will require any customer action (we should avoid any config changes customers must perform).

I'll notify the CS director and the SLA team that this was an org-tier reconciliation bug; we should capture a runbook step to detect similar merges proactively.

—Vanessa
Head of Sales Ops (Americas)
